text:
Recent research supports testing history dependence directly. [Does It Look Sequential? (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.12008) compares original and shuffled histories across 15 datasets, finding weak sequential structure in several popular benchmarks. [MIMAR-SRec (2026)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/38489) models multiple intent horizons and tests controlled interaction and temporal perturbations. Practical diagnostic proposal: compare equal-sized recent-history and older-history removals, recent-only versus older-only inputs, and order shuffling; measure candidate-score changes and top-10 overlap. Keep benchmark splits and selection metrics fixed. These probes reveal model sensitivity, not verified current user intent.

Semantic resemblance alone provides weak evidence for recommendation claims. [On the Factual Consistency of Text-based Explainable Recommendation Models (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.24366) reports high semantic similarity despite poor factual consistency. Proposed rubric: direct textual support, broad thematic connection, contradicted claim, or insufficient evidence. Require each asserted connection to cite specific history items and title/description passages. Compatibility claims need explicit supporting specifications; otherwise abstain. Ownership, fulfilled needs, and willingness to choose now remain unknown without direct feedback. Textual grounding also does not establish that the cited evidence drove the model’s prediction.

Validate the rubric through a small, independently double-annotated audit spanning all four categories and evidence levels. Record agreement, adjudicate disagreements, and inspect unsupported-claim and abstention errors before scaling automated judgments. This addresses methodological concerns identified in [Do My Eyes Deceive Me? (2025)](https://aclanthology.org/2025.inlg-main.4/), which surveys 64 studies and finds inconsistent hallucination definitions and human-evaluation practices. Human evidence judgments should remain separate from users’ actual preference feedback.
